messages:
Lina: Quick sync  proposal: introduce role-aliases as a thin indirection layer so product teams can map local role names -> canonical permissions. Goal: simplify cross-tenant integrations and make policy renames non-breaking.
Owen: How's this different from role ids? We already have numeric role ids and names.
Lina: Role-aliases are namespaced bindings like `alias:billing-reader` that map to a set of role ids or individual perms. Alias can be org-scoped or global. Teams reference aliases in configs/SDKs instead of raw role ids.
Tara: Migration concerns: aliases could hide privilege creep if owners map to broader role sets. Need guardrails.
Sam: Suggestion: aliases must declare their effective perm-set and an owner team. Changes to mapping require two-person review or an approval window for high-risk perms.
Lina: Agreed. Also add an immutable alias-version once it's used in a policy binding; you can create new version to change mapping, old version remains until bindings migrate. This avoids silent privilege shifts.
Owen: Runtime: middleware should resolve alias -> perms at auth-time. Cache lookups with TTL and a continuity plan for cache miss: fall back to last-known mapping and emit `auth.alias.stale` metric.
sec-bot: note: Compliance rule C-3 requires audit trail of both alias and resolved permission at time of access.
Tara: For cross-tenant impersonation (service A calls B on behalf of tenant X), aliases help, but we must ensure alias resolution respects tenant boundaries. A tenant-local alias must not map to global perms when invoked from another tenant.
Sam: Policy: allow alias resolution only within alias namespace: `tenant:alias` vs `global:alias`. If a caller lacks cross-tenant-scope, resolution fails. Add `delegate:alias` capability for connectors explicitly allowed to resolve cross-tenant aliases.
Lina: Dev experience: Console shows alias lineage and an "impact" view: list of bindings and downstream services using alias. Add CLI `rw auth alias export --format csv` and `rw auth alias migrate --to alias:v2` for bulk updates.
Owen: Testing: create an e2e harness that replays 30 days of auth logs resolving alias versions; run shadow mode to detect regressions before cutting over.
Tara: Rollout: 1) RFC + docs; 2) server-side support + cache; 3) Console + CLI; 4) shadow resolve for 4 weeks (log-only); 5) enforce mode with migration helpers.
Sam: Edge case: short-lived elevated perms via alias (just-in-time) for support sessions. We should require temporal alias flag and record `elevation.approved_by` in audit.
infra-bot: canary deploy started for alias-resolver middleware on eng-runtime at 1823456805, 2% hosts.
Lina: Next steps: I'll draft RFC update with alias schema, lifecycle rules, and compliance checklist. @Sam please outline approval workflow for temporal elevations.
